content:
hello formal conjectures team, so i've just seen that OpenAI have released a whole lot of preprints, 722 of them, some of which have lean formalisations.

without getting into discussion about the wider implications of this, i have a narrower question: i'm wondering about misformalisations that might exist in their formalisation work. Having worked with AI-generated lean code, there's often some discrepancy between the real human-language statement, and what the AI writes into lean (to put it mildly). I'd totally trust what's in the formal conjectures repo over the statements that their swarm would have produced.

So i'd be curious to know about conjecture statements that are in formal-conjectures, that are also in the OpenAI repo, and where they differ; and if they differ, whether that difference amounts to having formalised a different result than claimed

https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/pull/6898

Contains the ones that have a lean formalisation, would be great if you could review it.

I think in most cases it should be pretty easy to add the necessary glue and to check that we can upgrade the formal_proof using lean4 at ... links to formal_proof usingn formal_conjectures at ...
I did it for one problem that interested me (Borsuk counterexample in dim 9) and it worked.

I would not be so sure to trust the statements in formal conjectures more in every case: if you have a real proof of a statement often during the formalisation of the proof you can notice misformalisations of the statements that are hard to spot otherwise (even though we do our best)
also: respect for only just seeing those results, they have been discussed widely, to say the least...

I also created issues for the informal solutions see recent https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/issues?q=is%3Aissue+state%3Aopen+label%3A%22solution+found%22

Of course here one has to be more careful already 3 have been reatracted, i.e. are not claimed anymore to be solved

by "informal solutions", one means an OpenAI solution that does not have a lean formalisation?

(btw i did know about the existence of these preprints, i just didn't know they were released yesterday)

Barinder S Banwait said:

by "informal solutions", one means an OpenAI solution that does not have a lean formalisation?

yes (and this might be a moving target, since they might just release more formalisations and also other people spend tokens on it.
